parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national document/entry regime with a tier-1 state facilities law. Passports are locked to birth sex (X-marker barred; mismatch can trigger refusal or fraud review), a universal exposure every outed traveller carries. The division's July 2025 law reserves multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex, adds a private cause of action, and sits in a state with no gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime law; a comparable state already produced a documented arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward. Custody adds severe documented harm (birth-sex placement, conversion-therapy policies, immigration abuse). Mitigants are real but partial: no trans criminalisation, national hate-crime and employment protections, functioning courts issuing injunctions, marriage recognition, decriminalised same-sex conduct. Outcomes are exclusion, humiliation, service denial and custody degradation — not imprisonment for status or execution.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order and Feb 2025 cable lock passport/visa sex to birth sex, bar X-markers, and direct officers to refuse cases with document discrepancies or doubt about sex; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad; fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered but never automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver; litigation pending; entry not categorically barred for being trans.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into refusal or fraud allegation, then into detention or custody placement by birth sex.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented trespass arrest of a trans woman (Mar 2025) held 24 hours in a men's ward; national corrections bureau adopts conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts have enjoined several orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State facility law funnels into arrest → birth-sex custody, where federal custody policies apply on top.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law (eff. 1 July 2025) reserves all multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex, applies across public facilities and schools, and creates a private cause of action; four states criminalise use in some circumstances; national map shows growing bans in a majority of mapped categories.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Accommodation permitted where it involves no opposite-sex multi-occupancy access; 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; no enforcement actions under this division's law are documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exclusion is universal for an outed visitor in public buildings, transit hubs, stadiums and schools; interaction with private venues varies (bans on private settings in 6 states).

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors (2024) and restricts youth sports; national funding freeze, proposed public-insurance bar for under-18s, subpoena of under-19 patient records, and closure of LGBTQ youth crisis services; care denial in emergency for trans patients is not documented but the hostile climate raises the possibility.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned in the division; national employment discrimination protection survives; several orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
care_services.interaction: Travelling with a minor is materially riskier: a care-seeking family can become an investigated subject under the Jan 2025 law-enforcement order targeting schools and social transition.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo links 'radical gender ideology' to violent extremist framing; 66% public support for birth-sex markers signals broad social hostility, not mere friction.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never list gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; advocacy and litigation continue openly.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses discretionary scrutiny at checkpoints and facility enforcement, raising outing probability.

minors_guardians.exposure: School restroom mandate by birth sex with only non-use 'accommodation'; care and sports bans for minors; criminal-prosecution threat against teachers facilitating social transition creates a chilling, surveillance-adjacent environment for a visiting parent and child.
minors_guardians.protection: National employment protection and pending litigation; division school law applies to enrolled students, not transitory visitors in hotels or public venues.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family still meets the facilities law in every public restroom and lodging common area.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime statute and no state nondiscrimination law; national statistics show sexual-orientation bias consistently among reported hate incidents; four states flagged 'Do Not Travel'; 190+ anti-trans bills a year evidence a hostile climate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination prohibited nationally since 2020; three city ordinances cover gender identity; same-sex conduct legal since 1977.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists federally but state-level investigation quality and local police response are uneven and undocumented here.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division's facility law is unravelling in this inventory: no challenge or enforcement action sourced; state equality-tracking rates the division Negative with only the national employment protection noted.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple national orders blocked or enjoined; ACLU-style suit over passports pending; running legal-aid FAQ; national hate-crime and employment recourse operative.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Which measures are in force at the moment of travel is genuinely uncertain, so exposure varies by date.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than Vellandra: no Visitor Conduct Register or categorical entry bar for transgender visitors; refusal here requires a documented discrepancy or fraud analysis with waiver and pending litigation, not automatic exclusion of trans people as a class.

Closest match: routine universal exposure at checks and facilities, documented detention/humiliation, narrow and slow remedies, inconsistent enforcement, no credible imprisonment-for-status or execution — the same tier-1-plus-partial-recourse structure.

Higher than Kestrel Isles' administrative screening because severity exceeds missed connections: a private cause of action, a documented arrest with birth-sex ward placement, and federal custody conversion-therapy and immigration-abuse records push below the 0.55 friction tier.

Materially lower than Meridia: no trained respectful inspection, no tribunal appeal with compensation for detention, no X-marker acceptance, and the destination's own facilities law affirmatively excludes rather than merely questioning inconsistently.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous national exposure (birth-sex-locked documents, discrepancy-triggered refusal, active travel advisories from allied states) layered with one continuous state exposure (all multi-occupancy facilities reserved by biological sex, enforceable by private suit). If discovery escalates to police contact, the division's trespass pathway produced a documented arrest and a night in a men's ward, and federal custody layers conversion-therapy-style policies and documented immigration abuse — so severity climbs steeply with any detention. Protections are genuine but operate one level up: national hate-crime and employment law, injunctions, litigation, city ordinances. Law and public opinion are aligned against, so rule of law does not discount hostility; it mainly supplies partial, slow remedies. No criminalisation of trans status and no execution pathway keep this out of the lowest bands; tier-1 universal exposures keep it out of Reduced Risk.
